newsitem.title: USA: Bond market wrapup - late European trade.
newsitem.headline: Bond market wrapup - late European trade.

text.p: This is how major world bond markets looked at 1630 GMT on Friday.
UNITED STATES - The prices of U.S. Treasury securities were sharply lower at midday on Friday as strong employment and manufacturing reports took the wind out of the bond market's sails.

U.S. nonfarm payrolls rose by 316,000 in July, the government reported, against market expectations in the range of a rise of about 200,000. The unemployment rate also dropped to 4.8 percent, from 5.0 percent. Futures: September T-bonds at 115-3/32, down 1-21/32
September Eurodollars at 94.26, down 0.04
Cash: Long bond yield 6.43 percent.

GERMANY - Bund futures extend losses, sliding below support at 102.63 and 102.53, as U.S. debt falls following July NAPM data which spurred fears of inflation. Futures: September Bunds on LIFFE at 102.33, down 0.7
September Euromarks at 96.65, down 0.05
Cash: 10-year Bund yield 5.6 percent.
BRITAIN - UK gilts sank with U.S. Treasuries on Friday after an unexpected surge in the July non-farm payroll.

Traders said sentiment in the U.S. market has deteriorated markedly as a result of the payroll figures and a strong July NAPM survey, but gilts managed to outperform most of Europe. Futures: September Long gilts on LIFFE at 114.68, down 0.75
September Eurosterling at 92.66, down 0.06
Cash: 10-year gilt yield 7.01 percent.

FRANCE - French bond futures tumbled to their lowest level for two weeks on Friday after a slew of economic reports revived fears of U.S. interest rate rises while a fragile mark unsettled European interest rate futures.

Traders said the tone of the French market next week would depend very much on how the U.S. bond market ended the session and whether investors believed mark weakness would spur the Bundesbank to raise interest rates. Futures: September Long bond on MATIF at 129.98, down 0.22
September PIBOR at 96.45, down 0.02
Cash: 10-year bond (OAT) yield 5.54 percent.
ITALY - Italian bonds and Btp futures closed just off session lows, with futures sliding further in Liffe APT trading, dragged down by T-bonds on a raft of U.S. data.

Traders noted that while the thin Italian market fell on Thursday on profit-taking, losses in today's pre-weekend session were entirely due to the slump on the U.S. debt market. Futures: September Long bond on LIFFE at 136.25, down 0.78
September Eurolira at 93.29, down 0.01
Cash: 10-year bond (BTP) yield 6.52 percent.

JAPAN - JGBs cling to firm levels in London after clawing new highs in Japan aided by weak Tokyo shares. Dlr/yen retreats. Japan June trade numbers next week expected to be JGB-friendly. Futures: September JGB future on LIFFE compared with Tokyo close at 126.6, up 0.14
September Euroyen at 99.37, unchanged
Cash: 10-year JGB yield 2.32 percent.
EUROBONDS - Eurobond primary market activity was almost at a standstill on Friday and the quiet holiday mood was expected to continue next week.
"It is likely to be very quiet next week -- we have absolutely nothing in the pipeline," a syndicate head at a U.S. bank said.
